ev.q: CDC analyzed BRFSS data from 2005, 2007, and 2009
From 2005 to 2009, the overall percentage of adults screened for high blood cholesterol during the preceding 5 years increased from 72.7% to 76.0%
remains lower than the Healthy People 2020 target of 82.1%
was significantly higher among persons aged 45–64 years (88.8%) and ≥65 years (94.7%) than 18–44 years (63.2%)
remains lower than the Healthy People 2020 target of 82.1%
All reported percentages were age-standardized using the 2000 U.S. standard projected population
BRFSS is a state-based, random-digit–dialed telephone survey
Linear trends across survey periods were assessed using orthogonal polynomial coefficients
Healthy People 2020 monitors national progress related to screening and controlling high blood cholesterol

methods_quotes.q: Linear trends across survey periods were assessed using orthogonal polynomial coefficients, and results with a p-value <0.05 were considered significant.
All reported percentages were age-standardized using the 2000 U.S. standard projected population, distribution no. 8
Age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population; weighted estimates.
